Aulūkya-darśana
(‘Ulūka’s philosophy’)
------------------------------------------
The sage कणाद is the founder of the Vaiśeṣika system of philosophy, one of the six systems of इन्दिअन् फिलोसोफ्य्. Since he lived upon the grains picked up from the agricultural fields, (kaṇa = grain, ad = to eat) he came to be known as ‘Kaṇāda.’ It is said that he performed severe austerities to get the grace of शिव. Pleased with his devotion and faith, शिव appeared before him in the form of an ‘ulūka’ (an owl) and taught him this philosophy. Hence कणाद’s वैशेषिक दर्शन is also known as ‘Aulūkya-दर्शन,’ the philosophy revealed by शिव in the form of Ulūka or owl. Traditional writers of Indian Philosophical systems generally refer to the Vaiśeṣika school as ‘Kaṇāda-दर्शन’ or ‘Aulūkya-दर्शन.’
See VAIŚEṢIKA DARŚANA for details.
